text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Stock Exchange chief Wahib Shaer says government studying possibility of extending foreign ownership of shares. Says international banks and investment funds want to invest in Jordanian stock but there are no shares available. New stock exchange law will enable Jordanian firms to list on foreign exchanges and international firms to issue shares in Amman.
- Deputy Prime Minister Abdullah Ensour says administrative reform will be precisely carried out. Political considerations will not effect who gets jobs.
- Scandinavian experts recommend slight changes to Jordan's election law, increasing number of parliamentary seats to 120 from 80, but are split on whether to set quota for women.
- Foreign Minister Fayez al-Tarawneh says Jordan hasn't yet received an invitation from Egypt to attend a summit meeting.
- Cabinet to review proposed new elections law today which includes revisions to a number of constituencies.
- Ministry of Supply studies liberalising prices of some popular foods, possibly with a fixed ceiling, after prices of fruits, vegetables and chicken were floated.
- Trade and Industry Ministry secretary-general says it's important for Jordanian firms to be able to list on international bourses.
- Crown Prince Hassan and EU envoy Miguel Moratinos discuss Jordan-EU cooperation to rescue stalled Middle East peace process.
- Opposition voices objection to current election law but will participate in coming elections.
